articles.title: Rochdale Local Plan Advances with Focus on Housing and Transport
articles.excerpt: The Rochdale Local Plan aims to shape the borough's development until 2039, focusing on nearly 11,000 new homes and improvements to transport hubs.
articles.content_html:
A new strategy to shape Rochdale's future has moved closer to implementation as the borough's Local Plan is set to undergo public consultation. The plan outlines how Rochdale will develop until 2039, with a focus on building nearly 11,000 new homes and transforming local transport hubs.

The Local Plan, which has been refined into a 175-page document, was approved by council leaders and is expected to be formally adopted in 2027. Initially, the plan required 20 per cent of new housing developments to be affordable, but this threshold has been adjusted to 15 per cent due to financial viability concerns. Councillor Daniel Meredith stated that this change does not reflect a reduced commitment to affordable housing, highlighting that the council has delivered 883 affordable homes in the past five years, exceeding previous targets.

Housing is a significant component of the Local Plan, with designated land for new developments already identified through the Places for Everyone strategy, which aims to create around 175,000 homes across Greater Manchester over the next two decades. The plan is expected to stimulate investment and redevelopment in Rochdale, particularly through the Atom Valley scheme, which aims to create 7,000 new homes and 20,000 jobs.

The Rochdale Rail Corridor Strategy is central to the Local Plan, proposing the reconfiguration of land around transport hubs along the Manchester to Leeds railway line. This initiative aims to create vibrant spaces for living, working, and recreation, focusing on stations in Rochdale, Castleton, Mills Hill, Smithy Bridge, Littleborough, and a new Slattocks station. The plan also includes improvements to walking and cycling routes, park and ride facilities, and community spaces, all intended to enhance the local economy.

articles.title: Lift Out of Service at Central Park Tram Stop
articles.excerpt: The lift at Central Park tram stop towards Rochdale is currently out of service, affecting access for passengers. Alternative arrangements are in place for step-free access.
articles.content_html:
The lift at Central Park tram stop, which serves passengers travelling towards Rochdale via Oldham, is currently out of service. The disruption was reported on 29 July 2026 at 5:26pm and will remain in effect until further notice.

Passengers heading towards Oldham can access the Manchester-bound platform via lift from The Gateway and then use the track crossing to reach the Oldham-bound platform. This arrangement allows for step-free access despite the lift being unavailable.

Transport for Greater Manchester has apologised for any inconvenience caused by this disruption. Further information can be found on the Bee Network travel alerts page.

For more information and live updates, visit the Bee Network travel alerts page.

articles.title: Rochdale's Local Plan to Shape Future with Thousands of New Homes
articles.excerpt: Rochdale's Local Plan aims to build nearly 11,000 new homes and enhance transport hubs by 2039, with a council meeting set to discuss the proposal on July 28.
articles.content_html:
A council meeting is scheduled for July 28 to discuss the Rochdale Local Plan, which aims to shape the borough's future by 2039. The plan includes the construction of nearly 11,000 new homes and significant changes around transport hubs.

The Local Plan is part of a broader strategy called Places for Everyone, which has been adopted by nine out of ten Greater Manchester councils. This strategy envisions the development of around 175,000 homes across the city region over the next two decades, with Rochdale expected to see substantial investment and redevelopment.

Key features of the Local Plan include the Rochdale Rail Corridor Strategy, which proposes reconfiguring land around transport hubs along the Manchester to Leeds railway line. This initiative aims to create spaces for living, working, and leisure, focusing on stations in Rochdale, Castleton, Mills Hill, Smithy Bridge, Littleborough, and a new Slattocks station.

The plan also addresses various topics such as climate and energy, economic growth, housing, and sustainable transport. The town centre is identified as a principal focus for regeneration, with recent developments including the £20 million redevelopment of Rochdale Town Hall, which is expected to become a key tourist attraction. The Local Plan is set to be pushed through to the next phase before formal adoption following the council meeting.

articles.title: Green Party Candidate Geraldine Coggins Unveils Vision for Greater Manchester Mayoral Election
articles.excerpt: Geraldine Coggins, Green Party candidate for Mayor of Greater Manchester, has outlined her plans for affordable housing and transport improvements, including free bus travel for young people and an orbital bus service.
articles.content_html:
A Green Party candidate has outlined her vision for the Greater Manchester mayoral election, pledging to deliver 20,000 genuinely affordable homes and introduce free bus travel for young people if elected.

Geraldine Coggins, a councillor from Trafford, stated that her campaign focuses on taking Greater Manchester back from corporate interests. She plans to establish a programme called Homes for Greater Manchester, which aims to build 10,000 new homes and retrofit another 10,000, all offered at affordable rates. Coggins argued that this initiative would ultimately save taxpayer money by reducing reliance on temporary accommodation.

Coggins also proposed an orbital express bus service, named the B Orbit, which would connect towns across Greater Manchester, including Rochdale, Oldham, and Wigan. She emphasised the need for increased investment in areas outside Manchester city centre, which she believes has been neglected. Coggins described the free bus travel for those under 22 as a potential game changer for the region, promoting public transport as a normal and safe means of travel.

In addition to housing and transport, Coggins highlighted the importance of revitalising town centres and increasing funding for violence reduction initiatives. Her proposals include a £3 overnight visitor levy on hotel stays to support public transport improvements and the establishment of an empty shops team to help return vacant premises to use.
